narrative: Material PL1__ME5B64B7 exhibits lumpy demand (CV=0.40) with a statistically significant positive trend across 131 working days. One extreme lead-time outlier (9,201.55 days) was removed; the cleaned lead-time series shows moderate variability (CV=0.35, mean=4.20 days). The combined demand-and-lead-time uncertainty drives sigma_LTD to 725.54 units, requiring a safety stock of 1,194 units to achieve the 95% service level — nearly double the current SAP value of 605. An EOQ of 4,842 units is recommended, well above the MOQ of 726, reducing annual orders from ~156 to ~23 while remaining within the storage capacity of 7,308 units.

research_insights.selection_rationale: The (r,Q) policy is appropriate for this material: demand is lumpy but nearly continuous (99.2% non-zero days), lead times are moderate and reasonably stable, and a binding MOQ makes a fixed-Q approach natural. The reorder point r=3,018 triggers replenishment when stock falls to coverage for mean demand over lead time plus safety stock; Q=4,842 is set to the EOQ, balancing ordering and holding costs.
research_insights.boundary_risk: Low. The capacity gate is satisfied: safety_stock (1,194) + order_quantity (4,842) = 6,036, which is below max_storage_units (7,308). No binding constraint reduction was required.
research_insights.escalation_flag: None. MOQ (726) + safety_stock (1,194) = 1,920, well within the 7,308-unit storage limit. No infeasibility conflict.
